subject: Hosted API pilot: quickstart steps, endpoints, and rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@finovate.com>; Procurement <procurement@finovate.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pilot: quickstart steps, endpoints, and rate limits

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier today, and thanks for carving out time. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps for a Hosted API evaluation so your eng team can validate integration surface and performance: 

Recap (what we covered)
- Redwood Hosted API overview: same runtime used in Dedicated but fully managed (no infra ops).
- Demo highlights: streaming chat endpoint, embeddings, and per-key prefix caching.
- Typical migration paths: start with Hosted API pilot, then decide on Dedicated or Private VPC if you need reserved capacity or on-prem requirements.

Your stated priorities
- Proof-of-concept with real traffic patterns (concurrent requests, 1–2k QPS bursts)
- Data residency and audit logs for compliance team
- Clear rate-limit and token throughput expectations for budgeting

Proposed Hosted pilot (2 weeks) — what we’ll deliver
1) Hosted demo tenant & API key for a dedicated test pool (isolated from other customers).
2) Performance baseline report (latency P50/P95, token throughput) using a small synthetic load and sample prompts you provide.
3) Quickstart guide + sample code (see attached).
4) One SE office hours session (60 min) during pilot.

Ask from you
- Confirm you want to proceed with Hosted API pilot (yes/no)
- Provide 1–2 sample prompts or workloads we should run during baseline
- Any procurement/legal contacts we should loop in for the pilot T&Cs

Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf (quickstart + sample curl/SDK snippets), pilot-scope-MAP.xlsx (proposed milestones)

If that sounds good I’ll spin up the test tenant tomorrow and schedule SE hours with Sean. 

Best,

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear plan. We’re interested in the Hosted pilot as a first step. A few quick clarifying questions so we can scope: 

1) Rate limits & concurrency: can you confirm per-API-key concurrency and per-minute token caps for the Hosted plan you’d provision? We expect several parallel inference streams from our product (long-form generation ~4–6k tokens).
2) Data retention / logs: our compliance team needs to know retention window for request/response logs and what’s available in audit exports.
3) Region / residency: we need US-only hosting for now. Can the tenant be provisioned in us-west region?
4) Pricing: top-line estimate for a 2-week pilot (usage-based) and any refundable credits for a pilot evaluation.

If you can provide the above we’ll confirm sample prompts and loop in our security procurement contact.

—Alex

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@finovate.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pilot: quickstart steps, endpoints, and rate limits

Hi Alex — quick technical notes to answer Marissa’s and your questions below. I’ll keep it focused so your eng/security teams have concrete numbers to work with.

1) Rate limits & concurrency (Hosted test tenant we’ll provision)- Per-API-key concurrency: default 20 concurrent requests. Can request a temporary bump to 50 for pilot if you share expected concurrency window.- Per-minute token cap: 1,500,000 tokens/min by default for the test pool; we can set a hard cap per key (e.g., 250k tokens/min) if you want bounded spend.- Request size guidance: streaming endpoints support in-flight token windows up to 8k tokens in our hosted defaults; for longer context (up to 32k) we recommend splitting into a prefill + incremental generation pattern.

2) Endpoints & URLs- Base: https://api.redwood.ai/v1- Chat (streaming): POST /chat/stream- Completion: POST /completions- Embeddings: POST /embeddings

3) Data retention & logs- Request/response logs retained for 90 days in the hosted audit logs by default; we can extend retention for enterprise plans.- Audit exports: CSV/JSON exports via Console and a dedicated S3 export option for Private/Dedicated customers.- For the pilot we can enable request-level metadata logging (no PII by default) and provide a one-time export.

4) Region- We will provision the pilot tenant in us-west by default. All pilot traffic will stay in that region and the baseline report will reference region-specific latencies.

5) Billing estimate for pilot- If you stay within the suggested token cap (<=250k tokens/min peak) a 2-week pilot (moderate load tests + 1k–3k sample requests/day) typically falls under $3k–$7k usage. We can apply a small pilot credit upon agreement to offset initial spend; Marissa will handle the credit approval.

6) Attachments: I’m attaching a compact rate-limit matrix for common scenarios (single-key, multi-key, burst).

If you want, I can jump on a short technical sync with your infra lead tomorrow to review concurrency patterns.

—Sean
